A1.justification: Despite the new RePoseD title, both PDFs describe the same underlying research, with matching solver formulations, camera configurations and retained results. Both main texts and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original synthetic experiments and pose/focal-length evaluations on Phototourism and ETH3D.

after.justification: Section 4 and supplementary Section 7 report original evaluations on Phototourism, ETH3D and ScanNet, including solver, matching and optimization comparisons.

M1.justification: The core geometric solver formulations remain. v2 extends their estimation pipeline with reprojection-error scoring and refinement, with or without shift, and integration into hybrid RANSAC. The zero-shift configurations already appear in v1's solver tables; their expanded explanation and testing do not establish an entirely new solver family.

E1.justification: v2 adds ScanNet RGB-D evaluation for calibrated, shared-focal and different-focal cases (Tables 10, 12 and 15), while retaining Phototourism and ETH3D. Conversely, v1's synthetic evaluations covering controlled image/depth noise and pure-rotation scenarios disappear, including Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: v2 adds MadPose's affine-depth solvers as direct comparators for all three camera configurations and Mast3r's nonlinear optimization for focal-length comparisons. The existing P3P, Rel3PT, 3p3d, 4p4d and standard point-based solvers remain. These additions substantially strengthen comparison against competing estimation approaches.

E3.justification: The primary evaluation moves from GC-RANSAC without local optimization to PoseLib with local optimization; PoseLib already appeared in v1's appendix, but its stated threshold changes from 1 to 2 pixels. Phototourism changes from nine scenes/43,678 pairs to five scenes/24,750 pairs. v2 also adds hybrid protocols and iteration-budget sweeps, introduces RoMA/Mast3r matching, revises depth sources from eleven to five, and replaces separate real-data rotation/translation summaries with combined maximum pose error.

E4.justification: v1's numerical-stability and controlled noise-sensitivity studies are removed. v2 adds systematic comparisons of Sampson versus reprojection refinement, shift/scale modelling assumptions, iteration-dependent speed–accuracy tradeoffs, and Mast3r matches combined with MoGe depth. The inverse-depth comparison and selected fast-versus-GB results are retained, rather than newly introduced analyses.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 2 reports error distributions using medians and 25th/75th-percentile boxes; these statistical spread displays disappear with the synthetic experiments. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: v2 substantially replaces and expands the benchmark results. For example, its new Phototourism SP+LG/MoGe comparison reports 40.42 mAA at 23.41 ms for 3PTs00f1,2 versus 38.89 at 44.03 ms for 4PTsuvf1,2 (Table 5). These are new within-version comparisons, not demonstrated gains over v1 under identical settings. Supplementary Tables 6–7 retain selected v1 DA V2 results unchanged.

T1.justification: Most affine- and inverse-depth reasoning is retained or relocated. Limited mathematical revisions include replacing the calibrated 3PTs00 worked example with explicit shared-focal 3PTs00f constraints and removing an extra scale factor from the four-correspondence focal-length distance constraint. The configuration table also revises reported focal-solver solution counts.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on jointly estimating scale, shift and pose with state-of-the-art accuracy. v2 broadens the central contribution to determining when depth information and different estimation strategies help, explicitly emphasizing scale-only alternatives, RANSAC choices and efficiency against competing affine-depth solvers. The three camera configurations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial conditional interpretation: when shift modelling is unnecessary, when reprojection refinement can help with reliable indoor depths, and why hybrid RANSAC trades computation for accuracy. It also tentatively attributes declining accuracy at larger iteration budgets to physically implausible scale/focal solutions that current checks admit. Existing coplanarity and pure-translation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents Mast3r's 500 coarse/200 fine refinement iterations, its distinct CPU/GPU hardware, and exclusions from runtime measurements. Conversely, v1's statement that source code is available, accompanied by a URL, becomes only a promise of future public release in v2. This changes the documented access information without establishing the repository's actual status.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially revises positioning, especially by acknowledging Yu et al.'s concurrent MadPose work as solving the same affine-depth formulation. v2 distinguishes its contribution through solver efficiency, additional parameter configurations and conditional disagreement about shift modelling. It also expands discussion of DUSt3R/Mast3r and depth-assisted reconstruction research.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled RePoseD and extensively rewrites its abstract, introduction, contributions and experimental narrative. A dedicated Related Work section is introduced, method sections are consolidated, and inverse-depth material is moved into a separately organized supplement. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v1's stability and noise figures are replaced by a pipeline illustration and speed–accuracy plots. The solver-configuration tables are merged, and benchmark tables are extensively redesigned around matchers and optimization variants, with much denser supplementary displays. Selected unchanged DA V2 results are extracted into compact supplementary tables.

improvement.justification: Direct MadPose comparisons, systematic optimization and parameter-modelling controls, and ScanNet evaluation substantially strengthen the evidence for when depth-based estimation helps. Together with clearer positioning and more conditional conclusions, these address important limitations of v1's comparative argument. Removing synthetic stability/noise evidence and replacing the code URL with a future-release promise weaken verification, but the expanded controlled comparisons provide a substantial net improvement.
